subject: Evidence package request: isolation, snapshot purge and cross-region fallback behavior
messages:
From: Mike Hammond <mike.hammond@acmecorp.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acmecorp.com
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence package request: isolation + fallback behavior

Dylan,

Thanks for taking this on. Acme needs an evidence package for our upcoming compliance review that demonstrates how the Dedicated deployment serving our tenant behaves with regard to in-country routing, isolation, retention, and deletion. High-level asks below — target delivery window is 10 business days from today if possible.

Please include concrete artifacts where available rather than just policy language. Specifically we are requesting:

- A routing & enclave diagram showing the in-country routing policy and enforced egress restrictions for Acme tenant traffic.
- Description and sample logs showing the "replication fence" behavior (how/when replicas are allowed to cross regions) and any config flags that gate replication.
- Proof of snapshot purge when a tenant is deleted: audit log entries, snapshot chain hashes (pre/post purge), and timing (how long between delete event and physical snapshot removal).
- Evidence of ephemeral cache/kv invalidation after deletion or role-revocation (token invalidation or cache flush timestamps).
- A short failure-mode note: what happens if primary region fails — does traffic route to a read-only fallback, are writes blocked, and what are isolation guarantees during fallback? Example logs or a short reproducible test would be helpful.

Attachments or stubs are fine for large artifacts. Our DPO will review and may follow up with smaller clarifying asks.

-Mike
Mike Hammond
Security Operations Lead
AcmeCorp
security@acmecorp.com

From: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Mike Hammond <mike.hammond@acmecorp.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence package request: isolation + fallback behavior

Mike — thanks for the clear asks. We can assemble an evidence package that maps to each bullet. Proposed deliverables and timeline:

Delivery (by Tue, 2026-05-12):
1) Architecture & routing artifact: annotated diagram + config snippet for the routing policy that pins tenant egress to the US region and the in-enclave egress denylist.
2) Replication fence doc + sample scheduler logs: explanation of fence windows and a redacted log excerpt showing the fence enforced on a live snapshot.
3) Snapshot purge transcript: audit log entries for a synthetic delete (performed in our test tenant), pre/post snapshot hash listing, and a short note on retention windows.
4) Ephemeral cache purge evidence: KV invalidation token sample + timestamped cache flush event and the script we run for cache tombstone.
5) Failure-mode summary: a 1-page runbook showing fallback behavior (reads routing, write blocking, and isolation steps) plus a short test plan you can run with us if you want to validate.

We will attach an evidence-checklist.csv to this thread summarizing items and owners. Quick Qs before we start:
- Do you require signed attestation (e.g., PDF signed by our Security lead) or are raw logs sufficient for your review?
- Any specific PII/data redaction constraints on logs we should apply?

If you want, we can set up a 30-minute call Thursday to walk through the artifacts as we assemble them.

Thanks,

Dylan Brooks
Technical Account Lead, Dedicated Deployments
Redwood Inference

[attachment: evidence-checklist.csv]

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Mike Hammond <mike.hammond@acmecorp.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 10:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence package request: isolation + fallback behavior

Mike / team — adding the technical clarifications and a couple of small artifacts we'll attach.

Notes:
- Replication fence: operationally we gate cross-region replication with a two-step fence: (1) scheduling window + (2) manual unlock token. The token issuance is auditable; sample token issuance events will be included.
- Snapshot purge: snapshots are garbage-collected after tombstone propagation completes; the purge is a two-phase delete and we will include the pre/post snapshot manifest hashes. We will also include a sample audit log line for the delete event (redacted).
- Ephemeral cache/kv: our runtime emits a cache-invalidation token on delete events. The token is hash-bound to the tenant id + deletion timestamp; we will provide an example token and the invalidation timestamp.

Attachments included (stubs):
- scrub-playbook.txt (excerpt of the purge playbook and step-by-step commands)
- sample-audit-log.json (redacted audit entry + manifest hash sample)

Technical snippet (example of attestation command we run):

# generate-attestation --tenant acme-tenant-42 --event delete --out attestation-20260506.sig
# verify-attestation attestation-20260506.sig --trusted-root redwood-kms

We will not include raw PII in the logs; everything will be redacted per your DPO note unless you instruct otherwise.

Laura Bennett
Senior SRE, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

[attachment: scrub-playbook.txt]
[attachment: sample-audit-log.json]

From: Mike Hammond <mike.hammond@acmecorp.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, security@acmecorp.com
Date: Thu, 7 May 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence package request: isolation + fallback behavior

Thanks, Dylan / Laura — that plan looks good and the artifacts you listed are exactly what we need. Two quick asks before you package:

1) Please include a signed PDF attestation from your security lead for the snapshot purge item (we'll accept standard PGP-signed or a signed PDF).
2) Can you include a short proof-of-execution (3 steps max) we can run during the call to validate the cache invalidation behavior?

We will plan to join the Thursday call (please send a calendar invite) and the HubSpot record is ACME-12345 if you want to attach artifacts there.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

-Mike
Security Operations Lead
AcmeCorp
